messages:
emma: FYI I just finished HF->Redwood conversion for model hf/lorax-3b and saw a token count delta on inputs with decomposed accents (e + U+0301).
emma: Quick example I used to repro:
```
# original (precomposed)
input_A = "Café prices are up"
# decomposed (e + \u0301)
input_B = "Cafe\u0301 prices are up"
```
emma: HF tokenizer tokenized both as 6 tokens. Redwood converted tokenizer tokenized input_A as 6 but input_B as 8 (extra tokens inserted around the combining accent). :thinking_face:
arjun: can you paste the exact tokenized outputs and the conversion command you used?
emma: sure. conversion command: `redwood-convert --from hf --model hf/lorax-3b --out-dir /tmp/lorax-redwood`
emma: token dumps below:
```
# hf token ids for input_B: [128, 45, 67, 902, 11]  # (example, length 5)
# redwood token ids for input_B: [128, 45, 67, 9999, 77, 902, 11]  # length 7 -> weird special-token-ish id 9999 in middle
```
kai: that 9999 looks like a placeholder from the byte-fallback pretokenizer. Did the conversion pick a ByteFallback pretokenizer by default? :eyes:
emma: digging now — the HF tokenizer had `normalizer=null` in its JSON. The converter code currently forces `NFKC` unless `explicit_keep_normalizer` flag is set. So decomposed accents get normalized -> different byte fallback behavior.
arjun: ah, so we normalized compose/decompose which changed how bytes are mapped -> different byte fallback insertions. That explains the extra placeholder tokens. Did this affect evals?
emma: yes. Ran our quantization pipeline (8-bit) after conversion and saw ROUGE-L drop ~4.7% on the internal summarization evals where source text had many accented names. eval-bot: automatic_evals/quant-8bit/lorax-3b run FAILED quality threshold (delta rouge_l = -4.7%).
kai: Oof. This is a clear QA regression. Short-term patch: make the converter preserve the original HF normalizer when present. Can you try re-converting with `--keep-normalizer`?
emma: tried that locally: `redwood-convert --from hf --model hf/lorax-3b --keep-normalizer true` -> token counts match HF now, special id 9999 gone. Re-ran quant-8bit smoke -> rouge_l delta back to within noise (-0.2%).
arjun: good. For long-term: we should add a unit test in converter that asserts tokenization parity for both NFC and NFD variants of inputs for any model that has `normalizer=null` vs explicit normalizer.
kai: also log this as a model onboarding checklist item: "preserve HF normalizer or explicitly document conversion default". Might save other folks from silent regressions.
emma: filing a small PR: fix default to honor `tokenizer.json` normalizer if present; add smoke test that feeds decomposed accents + NBSP + ZWSP samples.
emma: attaching minimal reproduction (I pasted snippet to #eng-ml-private gist) :link:
arjun: if you want, I'll draft an eval regression ICC ticket and tag infra to block deploys for converted models until the converter has the flag toggled.
kai: nice. One more note: we should also audit chat templates—some of our chat-mode templates add a leading space before assistant role which interacts poorly with prefix-space handling in some tokenizers and can shift stop-token positions after quant. Put that on the checklist too. :memo:
emma: agreed. PR up in 10m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
